Performers
The Tudor Consort (vocal ensemble), Alastair Carey (director) Documented

The track description and Carey’s album notes agree. Five written parts do not establish five individual singers, and no instrumental players are credited.

[2] [3] [1]
Work version
Five-part unaccompanied vocal setting, SSATB Documented

The opened score supplies two soprano, alto, tenor and bass parts, without instruments. Neither the exact edition used by the choir nor its performance transposition is established.

[4] [5] [2]
Recorded
2005-11-02 Documented

The track names the Ordizia concert; the album’s first-person liner notes explicitly date it to Wednesday 2 November 2005. The 19 August 2010 date on FMA and Commons is an online release, not the recording session.

[2] [3]
Place
Parroquial Church, Ordizia, Spain Documented

The track and album notes name the venue. The later Rome concert and 2006 New Zealand recording described elsewhere in the same album notes belong to different tracks.

[2] [3] [1]
Label
Unknown Unknown

The album was prepared for the Tudor Consort’s twentieth anniversary, but no original imprint is named. FMA and Commons are access repositories.

[3]
Catalogue
Unknown Unknown

No commercial catalogue number is supplied.

[3]
Matrix, take, sides
Unknown Unknown

The notes refer to a disc but supply no matrix, mastering identifier or take number.

[3]
Transfer
Timothy Hurd, producer and engineer; Commons import by ComputerHotline Documented

Hurd is explicitly credited at album level. The Commons uploader is not presented as the original engineer.

[3] [1]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The 2005 concert date, 2010 FMA release and 11 April 2020 Commons upload do not establish a mastering or transfer date.

[2] [3] [1]
Processing
FMA MP3 source converted to Ogg for Commons; Wikimedia MP3 access derivative Documented

Original recording medium, microphones, editing and equalisation settings are not supplied. No further processing or audio trim is introduced here.

[1] [2]
Composition rights
Public-domain 1603 madrigal; inspected engraving dedicated under CC0 Documented

Historical composition rights and Van Gilst’s engraving status are separate from the Tudor Consort’s sound recording rights.

[4] [5]
Recording rights
Rule 1 — CC BY 3.0 Unported Documented

The external FMA track was opened directly and explicitly licenses this human choral performance under CC BY 3.0, without a NonCommercial condition. Commons contains a 2024 review template referring anomalously to a Flickr image; that text is not relied upon as verification of an FMA recording. The actual FMA recording page supplies independent evidence.

[2] [3] [1] [7]

Monteverdi, Quel augellin che canta, SV 87; The Tudor Consort, directed by Alastair Carey. Recorded live, Parroquial Church, Ordizia, Spain, 2 November 2005. Timothy Hurd, producer and engineer. Source: The Tudor Consort / Free Music Archive; Commons import by ComputerHotline. Recording CC BY 3.0; transcoded access copy, no new editorial audio cut. Rights statement

  1. Wikimedia Commons — Tudor Consort, Quel Augelin Che Canta — Ordizia and Carey credits, FMA source, CC BY licence, 2010 Date field, 2020 upload and anomalous Flickr-worded review template.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  2. Free Music Archive — Claudio Monteverdi: Quel Augelin Che Canta — Recording description, Ordizia venue, Alastair Carey, Released 19 August 2010 and explicit CC BY 3.0 recording licence.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  3. Free Music Archive — The Tudor Consort, Live in Concert — Alastair Carey’s liner notes identify the first group of tracks with Wednesday 2 November 2005 in Ordizia; distinguish later Rome and New Zealand sessions; name Timothy Hurd as producer and engineer.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  4. IMSLP — Quel augellin che canta sì dolcemente, SV 87 — Book IV, No. 13, 1603 publication, five unaccompanied voices, Guarini source and Daniel Van Gilst’s 2019 CC0 edition.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  5. Monteverdi — Quel augellin che canta, ed. Daniel Van Gilst — All four pages viewed: upper-trio opening, later lower-part entries, longer middle-span values and final moving upper figures over sustained lower parts. Used for texture, not exact timing or sounding pitch.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  6. LiederNet — Quel augellin, che canta — Guarini, Il pastor fido, Act I, scene 1, lines 175–⁠186; marks differences in Monteverdi’s adapted words. No modern translation is reproduced.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  7. Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Unported — Licence linked directly by the FMA track for the recording.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
